summary.intent: Implement SDK-driven E2E and load test suites for CipherBox that bypass browser automation overhead, using CipherBoxClient programmatically against a real API stack.
summary.outcome: Created two new workspace packages (tests/sdk-e2e with 83 passing tests across 10 suites, tests/load with 5 load scenarios), implemented a throttle bypass header mechanism, fixed three correctness bugs discovered during the test run, and validated load tests against the local stack.

repo: setApiClientConfig in packages/api-client/src/instance.ts is a module-level singleton used by all orval-generated API functions — multi-account tests must serially switch this singleton between accounts, contaminating later test suites if not re-set.
The ThrottlerGuard is applied per-controller via @UseGuards(), not globally via APP_GUARD — each controller must be individually updated to swap the guard class.
Per-endpoint @Throttle() decorators exist on the IPNS publish endpoint (10 publishes/min) in ipns.controller.ts, stricter than the controller-level limit (10 req/s, 100 req/min).
NestJS ConfigModule loads .env files which override shell environment variables — setting NODE_ENV=test in the shell does not override NODE_ENV=development in .env.
The ClaimInviteDto has @MinLength(258) on encryptedKey, requiring at least 129-byte ECIES ciphertext — dummy Uint8Array(64) payloads fail DTO validation with a 400.
The API's /shares endpoints return encryptedKey as a hex string, but @cipherbox/crypto's unwrapKey() expects Uint8Array — requires hexToBytes() conversion in callers.
pnpm --filter api dev uses NestJS watch mode which hot-reloads on file save, making env var changes take effect without a full restart.
The integration test at packages/sdk/src/__tests__/integration.test.ts lines 24-59 is the canonical pattern for test-login → vault init → CipherBoxClient construction.

code.finding: Module-level _config singleton and _cachedInstance — all orval-generated functions share one axios instance, making true multi-account parallel operation impossible without the singleton refactor todo.
@Throttle({ default: { limit: 10, ttl: 60000 } }) on publish endpoint is the direct cause of load test 429s — 10 IPNS publishes/min per IP is hit immediately under concurrent load.
ThrottlerModule configured with limit:10/ttl:1000 and limit:100/ttl:60000 — these are the controller-level defaults; per-endpoint @Throttle decorators can be stricter.

Multi-account test fixtures overwrite setApiClientConfig singleton — suites running after share-operations or invite-link must re-call setApiClientConfig before operations that use sdk-core IPNS functions.

workflow: Using replace_all or sed for multi-occurrence pattern replacement across files with nested brackets is fragile — mismatched parens corrupted vault-lifecycle.test.ts and required a full rewrite.
crypto.getRandomValues() has a hard 65536-byte limit per call — generating test data above 64KB requires chunked fills.
Background Bash tasks with git commit can hang waiting for 1Password SSH agent if the agent connection has timed out — running the commit directly (non-background) avoids the hang.
The pnpm-workspace.yaml tests/* glob picks up new test packages automatically — no explicit workspace registration needed, only pnpm install.
Promise.allSettled is the right concurrency primitive for load test client pools since the bottleneck is network I/O not CPU, and per-client test accounts mean each has its own auth token closure.

friction: API rate limiting (10 req/s, 100 req/min) blocked the entire SDK E2E test run before the bypass header was implemented — required a temporary NODE_ENV=test workaround to unblock.
1Password SSH agent timed out during background commit tasks, causing multiple hung git commit processes that had to be killed and retried.

The fetchHeaders/testFetch helper was introduced mid-session due to raw fetch calls in 3 test suites not automatically inheriting the axios defaultHeaders — required iterating through multiple approaches before settling on testFetch.
TypeScript rootDir restriction in tests/load/tsconfig.json prevented importing from tests/sdk-e2e — required adding paths/rootDirs override.
The sed replace_all approach corrupted vault-lifecycle.test.ts (mismatched closing parens from fetchHeaders wrapping) requiring a full file rewrite.
Load test error swallowing (catch with no logging) made diagnosing the crypto.getRandomValues() failure opaque — had to add temporary console.error to find the root cause.
open_items: Refactor @cipherbox/api-client to instance-scoped axios: configure orval to generate functions that accept an axios instance parameter, thread through sdk-core SdkContext — eliminates singleton, multi-account switchTo hack, cross-suite contamination, testFetch helper, and defaultHeaders workaround. Tracked in .planning/todos/pending/2026-03-22-refactor-api-client-from-singleton-to-instance-scoped-axios.md

Investigate @Throttle decorator bypass gap: the BypassableThrottlerGuard subclasses ThrottlerGuard so per-endpoint @Throttle decorators should use the same guard instance — verify whether IPNS publish 429s during load tests are from the throttler or from IPFS upstream. Tracked in .planning/todos/pending/2026-03-22-investigate-throttle-bypass-gap-for-per-endpoint-throttle-decorators.md

Raw fetch calls in vault-lifecycle, share-operations, and invite-link test suites should be migrated to use the generated API client functions — currently patched with testFetch wrapper, natural follow-on to the api-client singleton refactor.
Load test scenarios against staging need STAGING_THROTTLE_BYPASS_SECRET set as a GitHub Actions secret before the load-test.yml workflow can run end-to-end.

The load test client pool creates accounts serially in batches of 5 — with the api-client singleton limitation, all clients currently share one baseUrl/token config; true per-client isolation awaits the singleton refactor.
Staging load tests can only validate single-node throughput; production horizontal scaling validation requires a separate multi-source-IP strategy documented in tests/TESTING_STRATEGY.md.
